saved_evidence.title: Esperanza bicycle repair: rear derailleur adjustment
saved_evidence.description: Printable step-by-step instructions from the City's Esperanza bicycle programme for adjusting a rear derailleur, one of a set of repair guides the programme publishes.

text_excerpts.1:
Inspect hanger and derailleur 
for damage.  Turn barrel       
adjustor clockwise until snug. 
Adjust high limit screw (H) until 
upper pulley is in line with 
smallest (outer) cog. 
Keeping cable taut, secure using 
bolt/nut. Look for a groove to in-
dicate proper routing. 
Test indexing by shifting one 
click while turning crank, ob-
serve if chain shifts. 
If chain did not move onto the 
next cog, turn barrel adjuster 
counterclockwise until it shifts. 
Shift up and down through 
gears while turning crank, ob-
serve if chain shifts smoothly. 
If chain hesitates when shifting 
to larger (lower) gears, adjust 
barrel adjustor counter-
If chain hesitates when shifting to 
smaller (higher) gears, adjust bar-
rel adjustor clockwise. 
Repeat steps 4 through 8 until 
shifting is smooth, then shift to  
the largest (inner) cog. 
Tighten low limit screw (L) until 
derailleur moves slightly out, 
then back screw off 1/4 turn. 
Cut cable using cable cutters, 
leaving about 1.5 inches of ca-
ble after pinch bolt. 
Crimp a cable cap onto end of 
cable using pliers. 
Rear Derailleur Adjustment 
Indexed

saved_evidence.description: Printable step-by-step instructions from the City's Esperanza bicycle programme for removing a wheel from a single-speed bicycle, the companion to the multi-speed guide.

text_excerpts.1:
If wheel has a brake arm, re-
move brake arm bolt.  Place 
bolt somewhere safe for reuse. 
If the bike uses hand brakes, 
release brake caliper to allow 
tire to pass brake pads. 
Using a wrench (15mm is     
standard) loosen axle nut on both 
sides of axle.  
Allow the wheel to slide forward 
in the dropout. Remove chain 
from rear cog and hang on frame. 
Remove wheel from bicycle. 
Once repair is complete, return 
wheel to dropouts. Ensure cog 
is on right (drive) side of bike. 
If hub has a coaster brake, 
loosely reattach brake arm. 
Place chain on teeth of front 
and rear cogs. Chain should 
still hang loose between cogs.  
Holding the wheel centered, 
pull back until chain is tight. 
Tighten the left (non-drive) nut. 
Adjust chain tension by pushing 
front of wheel right (tighten) or 
Tighten right (drive) nut. Test 
chain tension by pedaling back-
Reconnect hand brakes and/or 
tighten coaster brake arm bolt. 
Test brakes for effectiveness. 
Single Speed Wheel  
Removal/Replacement

saved_evidence.title: Esperanza bicycle repair: wheel removal, multi-speed
saved_evidence.description: Printable step-by-step instructions from the City's Esperanza bicycle programme for removing a wheel from a multi-speed bicycle, the companion to the single-speed guide.

text_excerpts.1:
Shift rear derailleur until chain 
rests on highest (smallest) cog. 
If bike uses linear pull brakes, 
release brakes by removing 
brake noodle from stirrup. 
If bike uses cantilever brakes, 
disconnect straddle cable on non
-bolted brake arm.  
If wheel is bolted on, use a 
wrench (15mm is standard) loos-
en axle nut on both sides of axle.  
If wheel is a quick release, open 
cam lever on skewer. 
Pivot rear derailleur toward back 
of bike, allow wheel to drop down 
and remove from bike. 
Once repair is complete, return 
wheel to frame. Ensure cog is 
on right (drive) side of bike. 
Tighten axle nuts/close quick 
release. Quick release should 
require some force to close. 
If bike uses linear pull brakes, 
return noodle to stirrup to re-
connect brakes. 
If bike uses cantilever brakes, 
connect straddle cable to non-
bolted brake arm. 
Test wheel retention/bearing 
adjustment by moving wheel 
laterally and feeling for play. 
Pedal bike to test for brake rub, 
shift through gears to ensure all 
components are aligned. 
Multi-Speed Wheel  
Removal/Replacement
